content.comment_body: I'm having issues with the temperature curve spreadsheet included in [product_name] examples. Can someone advise the proper gain and offset settings for [article_no] so the water supply setpoint matches the outside air temperature values listed below (all temperatures in Fahrenheit)? At 90°F outside air: water supply 130°F At 80°F outside air: water supply 135°F At 70°F outside air: water supply 140°F At 60°F outside air: water supply 145°F At 50°F outside air: water supply 150°F At 40°F outside air: water supply 155°F High limit cutoff: don’t exceed 160°F Alternatively, these water supply setpoints: At 90°F outside air: water supply 130°F At 80°F outside air: water supply 140°F At 70°F outside air: water supply 145°F At 60°F outside air: water supply 150°F At 50°F outside air: water supply 155°F At 40°F outside air: water supply 160°F

Hello [user_name], and welcome to the forum. Your post is in the wrong section—the moderators will likely move it to the correct [product_name] board. Could you clarify your request? The settings for the analog amplifiers [article_no] are specified in Celsius, not Fahrenheit.

For these temperature values, the recommended settings in [article_no] are: Gain: -0.5 Offset: 1750 To apply a cutoff at 1600, use an analog threshold trigger along with an analog multiplexer, since a simple amplifier block can’t achieve a non-linear cutoff.

That was very helpful! So, to achieve the following: At 90°F outside air: water supply 130°F At 80°F outside air: water supply 140°F At 70°F outside air: water supply 145°F At 60°F outside air: water supply 150°F At 50°F outside air: water supply 155°F At 40°F outside air: water supply 160°F I would change the gain and offset in [article_no] to: Gain: -0.5 Offset: 1800 Thanks again.

You can adjust the settings as you prefer, but it won't resolve the issue. The water setpoint increments are not linear—there’s a 10-degree step between the first two points but only 5 degrees between the others.

analysis.insight_summary: Users are facing difficulties correctly configuring temperature setpoints using spreadsheet examples and analog amplifier blocks associated with [product_name], mainly due to confusion between Fahrenheit and Celsius units and the need for non-linear mapping. There is uncertainty regarding how to achieve the desired control curve and how to apply high limit cutoffs using available configuration tools.
analysis.user_expectations: The user hopes for an easy solution that allows outside air temperatures (in Fahrenheit) to be mapped directly to water supply setpoints—both with linear and non-linear curves—using analog block parameters and example resources for [product_name]. The solution should also incorporate a high limit cutoff.
